elements.element: Customer may assign without consent to an affiliate
elements.evidence: The Company may assign this Agreement ... without consent to an affiliate

elements.element: Customer may assign without consent to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets
elements.evidence: or to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all of its assets

elements.element: Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent
elements.evidence: HDI may not assign this Agreement ... without the prior written consent of the Company

elements.element: Consent not to be unreasonably withheld
elements.evidence: (which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld)

elements.element: Vendor may never assign to a Customer competitor
elements.evidence: and in no event to a competitor of the Company

elements.element: No Vendor termination right on Customer's change of control
elements.evidence: No change of control of the Company shall give HDI any right to terminate ... this Agreement

elements.element: Mutual right to assign to successors
elements.evidence: HDI may not assign this Agreement ... without the prior written consent of the Company
no notice mechanic appears in the inserted text

elements.element: Consent for other assignments not unreasonably withheld
elements.evidence: (which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld)

reasons: All six atomic preferred elements are present: Customer affiliate and successor assignment free of consent, a reasonableness-qualified consent gate on Vendor assignment, an absolute competitor bar, and no Vendor termination right on Customer change of control.
Fallback is not satisfied on its own terms (no mutual successor-assignment right and no written-notice mechanic), but the locked target is preferred, which is met.

Minimality fails: the edit re-states the entire untouched original sentence rather than anchoring a concise insertion, and it adds protection beyond the preferred position by barring suspension and re-pricing on change of control and by repeating 'in whole or in part' in both new sentences.
Intent is preserved: the original binding-on-successors sentence remains effective, all defined terms (Company, HDI) resolve, and no contradiction or dangling mechanic is introduced.
